alex: FYI seeing steady memory growth on a long-context Llama MQA run after we bumped rope scaling to 1.5x. Not a one-off — reproduces on CPU and GPU variants, long sessions >50k tokens. Paging shows lots of small evicts instead of coalesced pages.

maria: can you paste the exact run config + a tiny repro? is this with kv-paging enabled or the fallback path? :thinking:

sam: repro below — short script that drives a long single-session gen. Note the `kv_page_evictions` counter keeps ticking even when model is idle (only input prefixes).

sam: ```
# repro loop (simplified)
python stress_kv.py --model llama-70b-mqa-rope1.5 --seq 512 --long-prefix 60000 --batch 1 --kv-paging on
# telemetry excerpt (perf counters)
kv_pages_allocated=12048
kv_pages_evicted=5732
kv_reuse_hits=182
kv_fragmentation_pct=27.4
# observed heap: +3.2GB over 100k tokens
```

kiara: hmm. that fragmentation pct seems high. could be slot aliasing introduced by the MQA layout combined with rope scaling shifting hashed positions — pages aren't being reused because the rope-offset math changes cache keys. saw something similar on Mistral but with different eviction patterns.

alex: exact stack: runtime v2.8.1, kernel selector enabled, default batching heuristics. We tried kernel=force-quant and force-fp, same drift. Perf traces point at a lot of small DMA copies during page compaction.

perf-bot: attached trace <https://perf.redwood/trace/3178901234|trace-3178901234> (span: kv/paging/compaction)

maria: quick theory: rope scaling changes token-to-slot mapping, so previously contiguous KV slots get scattered -> increases fragmentation and prevents page coalescing heuristics from merging nearby entries. When we combined that with MQA interleaving, coalesced eviction can't find contiguous live blocks.

sam: confirmed with an instrumented run — added slot_index and page_owner logs. When rope_scale != 1.0 we see non-monotonic slot jumps every ~256 tokens. That pattern breaks our existing "adjacent-page merge" heuristic which expects monotonic locality.

kiara: two quick mitigations to try:
- conservative: pin rope_scale to 1.0 for long-session routing for MQA Llama (hotfix)
- long-term: update page-merge heuristic to use a rolling-window locality metric (instead of strict adjacency) and prefer merge if reuse probability > threshold.

alex: also noticed batching heuristics exacerbate it — many small single-request batches keep touching new prefixes which trigger allocation before compaction runs. If we increase batch_coalesce_window from 5ms -> 30ms reuse improves.

maria: action items:
- alex: open ENG ticket w/ perf trace + small repro (please include slot_index dump) — assign to eng-runtime (due EOD)
- sam: prototype rolling-window merge heuristic (bench on qwen/mistral/llama)
- kiara: experiment with batch_coalesce_window and report perf/latency tradeoffs
- ops: consider temporary routing rule to avoid rope-scale !=1.0 for long-lived sessions

alex: I'll open the ticket now: <https://redwood/issues/ENG-4578|ENG-4578> and drop the trace + logs. assigning to @sam. thanks all :thumbsup:
